text: Given a domain id, a date range, and direction=inbound, the message-stats tool returns only inbound per-user summaries.
evidence: pytest -v PASSED, confirms inbound_summaries/outbound_summaries are always lists (never collapsed to a bare dict when there's exactly one entry -- the ambiguity a naive generic XML-to-dict converter would get wrong, see api_client.py's module docstring).
notes: The test fixture includes both directions (matching the vendor's undirected example response); the direction=inbound query-param itself is passed straight through to the vendor per api_client.py's get_user_message_stats signature and is not separately asserted on the wire. Low risk: it is one of six uniformly-handled query params.

text: Given a domain id with one allow rule and one block rule, listing with rule_type=block returns only the block rule.
evidence: pytest -v PASSED. Parses both rule types from the vendor's own documented example; rule_type filtering itself is a query-param passed straight through to the vendor (same low-risk note as TC22).

text: Given a domain id, adding one block rule and then listing the rules shows it present.
evidence: pytest -v PASSED, confirms the add call posts <address>spam.example.com</address> to the create endpoint. The "then listing shows it" half requires a stateful mock (or a live account) -- not meaningfully provable against a stateless mock; deferred to TC35's live-account pass.

text: Given a domain id, calling the remove path with an empty rules list is rejected by the tool itself before any call reaches the vendor's destroy-rules endpoint.
steps: Start the service locally with a mocked api_client fixture pre-loaded with two rules
Observe the tool's response and the mocked client's call log
expect: The tool returns an invalid_argument error and the mocked client records zero calls to the destroy-rules endpoint
evidence: pytest -v: tests/test_tools.py::test_tc25_remove_empty_rules_list_is_rejected_before_any_vendor_call PASSED. Asserts both the invalid_argument error and respx route.call_count == 0 for the destroy_rules endpoint.
notes: Automated rather than run manually: this service has no console/UI to click through (it's an MCP tool), so "manual" execution is itself just an isolated call to the tool function -- which is exactly what this pytest test does, with the added benefit of a durable regression check. Judgment criteria unchanged from design.

evidence: pytest -v PASSED. Asserts against what api_client actually sent on the wire (decoded Basic-auth username) for two interleaved asyncio tasks, not just the final output -- this is what would catch a real global/module-level credential leak, per the SOP's stated concern.

text: Given a request to /mcp with no X-Mailprotector-Auth-Token header, the response is 401 and the body lists the required header, before any outbound call to Mailprotector.
evidence: pytest -v PASSED. Drives the real ASGI app end-to-end (httpx.ASGITransport), asserts HTTP 401 and that the body names X-Mailprotector-Auth-Token.

text: Given a real Mailprotector manager token, running initialize -> tools/list -> tools/call for mailprotector_list_domains against the live API returns a well-formed result.
steps: Obtain a real manager auth token from whoever owns a Mailprotector demo/test account
Run the service locally with that token in X-Mailprotector-Auth-Token
Call initialize, then tools/list, then tools/call mailprotector_list_domains
expect: tools/list shows 20 tools; tools/call returns 200 with a well-formed domain list (or an empty list if the test account has none)
evidence: Not run: no real Mailprotector account/token is available on this machine. Everything reachable without a live account was verified instead: `uv run python -m mailprotector_mcp` + `curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp -H 'X-Mailprotector-Auth-Token: placeholder' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'` returned HTTP 200 with all 20 tools (stateless -- no prior initialize handshake required), and the same request with the header omitted returned HTTP 401 listing X-Mailprotector-Auth-Token. See Self-test section for the full transcript.
notes: Needs a real vendor account; not available at design or dev time. Per references/mcp-track.md section 3 ("完成标准"), this does not block delivery to 6b.
